reason: The L-F2 drag host is now a real control and needs a Korean accessible name plus Korean copy/copy-failed status chips. ko.ts is a serialized collision root, so the lane ships the English fallback in web/src/console/objectcard/strings.ts (objectCardA11yStrings) and requests the Korean wire-up here.

keys.usage: aria-label of the object-reference drag host (ObjectCard header code + every relation row).
StatusChip tone=ok role=status after a successful clipboard write.
StatusChip tone=danger role=alert when navigator.clipboard rejects.

apply_notes: Add the block with `satisfies ObjectCardA11yStrings`, matching the existing `objectcardDyn` block's style.
No lane-side change is needed after the wire-up: objectCardA11yStrings() already prefers ko.console.objectcardA11y and only falls back to English when the key is absent.

Do NOT widen ObjectCardDynStrings to carry these keys — ko.console.objectcardDyn has a `satisfies ObjectCardDynStrings` clause, so widening that interface forces a ko.ts edit from every lane that adds a dynamic-layer string. The separate namespace is what keeps ko.ts serialized.
web/src/console/objectcard/ObjectCard.test.tsx reads the strings through the accessor, not through literals, so the tests pass unchanged before and after the wire-up.
